All your data has been deleted. Restart the app.
This action is IRREVERSIBLE. Everything goes: sessions, meals, photos, Shreddy conversations, API keys, settings. Existing backups in your cloud are NOT touched (you can restore later).

ShredCoach stores your data (sessions, meals, photos, conversations) only on your phone. No ShredCoach server receives your information. The only exceptions: Shreddy AI (chat) and meal/body scans, which send your text or photos to third-party AI providers (Groq, OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Mistral) that you explicitly choose in settings.
[TO COMPLETE: name, legal entity, address, GDPR email of the data controller. e.g. Sitou — contact@example.com]

Data stored locally on your device:
• Profile: first name, last name, age, weight, goals, level, injuries
• Sessions: exercises, sets, weights, duration, history
• Nutrition: meals, macros, scans, program
• Shreddy AI conversations: your messages and replies
• Photos: progression photos, meal scans, gym scans

Purposes: support your cut, compute your stats, personalize recommendations.

When you use Shreddy (chat) or an AI scan, your message or photo is sent directly (no ShredCoach intermediary) to the provider you chose. You provide your own API key. Providers have their own policies:

• Groq (United States) — https://groq.com/privacy-policy
• OpenAI (United States) — https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy
• Anthropic Claude (United States) — https://www.anthropic.com/privacy
• Google Gemini — https://policies.google.com/privacy
• Mistral (France) — https://mistral.ai/terms/

These non-EU transfers rely on Art. 49.1.a GDPR (explicit consent). You can refuse: the app works without these features.

If you enable backup, ShredCoach writes a ZIP archive into the folder YOU choose (Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, local). The contents and security of that folder depend on the provider you selected — their policy applies to the archive. ShredCoach does not read the archive after writing.

• **Access**: you can export all your data via Settings > Backup > Backup now (open JSON archive + readable photos).

• **Rectification**: edit your data directly in the app.

• **Erasure**: Settings > Delete all my data. Everything is wiped from the phone in one atomic operation.

• **Portability**: backup archive is open JSON + JPEG photos.

• **Objection / consent withdrawal**: disable Shreddy or AI scans in settings to stop transfers to third-party providers.

Data stays on your phone as long as you use the app. You can wipe it any time via Settings. When you uninstall the app, Android automatically deletes all local data (except backups you exported to your cloud).

Your AI API keys are encrypted via Android Keystore (AES-256-GCM, hardware-backed on most devices). Network traffic uses TLS 1.2+. The Room database is protected by Android disk encryption (FBE) if enabled on your device.
ShredCoach uses NO cookies, NO trackers, NO analytics tools. No advertising.
If you believe ShredCoach handles your data improperly, you can contact the controller (see section 1) or file a complaint with your local data protection authority (e.g. CNIL in France — cnil.fr).
This policy may evolve. Any substantial change will trigger a consent refresh on the next app launch.

Animated demonstrations in the exercises database (tap to see the move)
Back flat against the seat. Feet centered on the platform, shoulder-width. Descend to at least 90°. NEVER lock your knees at the top.
High feet = glutes, low feet = quads.
Squat rack + Olympic bar (45 lb empty).
Bar on traps. Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Descend until thighs are parallel. Back straight, drive through your heels.
King of all exercises. Minimum 3 sec on the descent.
Big step forward, back knee grazes the ground. Front knee should not go past the toes. Torso upright.
Add dumbbells once it gets too easy.
Leg extension machine. Knees aligned with the rotation axis.
Seated, fully extend your legs. Squeeze the quads for 2 sec at the top. Controlled 3-sec descent.
Perfect finisher after squat or leg press.
Leg curl machine. Lie face-down, ankles under the roller.
Curl your knees toward the glutes. Squeeze for 2 sec at the top. Very slow descent (3 sec). Hips stay glued to the bench.
Most neglected zone. Slow descent is the key.
Standing, bar in front of thighs. Hinge at the hips, pushing the glutes back. Back FLAT. Lower to mid-shins. Stand back up squeezing the glutes.
Excellent for glutes + hamstrings. Flat back is mandatory.
Floor mat. Advanced variant: back on a bench + bar across the hips.
Lying down, knees bent, feet on the floor. Drive the hips toward the ceiling. Squeeze glutes for 2 sec at the top.
Activates the glutes better than the squat. Progress to barbell hip thrust.
Seated leg curl machine. Thighs locked in, ankles on the roller.
Curl knees under the seat. Squeeze for 2 sec. Controlled return.
Hits the hamstrings from a different angle than the lying curl.
Chest press machine (converging or guided). Seated, handles at chest height.
Back flat against the seat. Push the handles forward. Don\'t lock the elbows. Controlled return.
Perfect to start with. Safe, no spotter needed.
Flat bench + bar rack. Olympic bar 45 lb.
Shoulder blades retracted, feet on the floor. Lower the bar to the mid-chest (2 sec). Pause 1 sec. Press up (2 sec). Never bounce.
The king pec exercise. Use a spotter on heavy sets.
Floor. Variants: incline push-ups (hands on bench = easier), decline push-ups (feet on bench = harder).
Hands shoulder-width + 4 in. Body braced. Lower chest to the floor. Push back up to extension. Elbows at 45°.
If 20+ reps feel easy, switch to weighted (backpack) or decline push-ups.
Cable crossover (two facing pulley columns). High or middle handles.
Arms out wide, elbows slightly bent. Bring hands together in an arc in front of you. Squeeze pecs for 2 sec.
Carves the separation between the pecs. Contraction beats heavy load.
Incline chest press machine (if available) or Smith machine + incline bench.
Same movement as the chest press, but at an incline angle. Press up and slightly forward.
Lower dumbbells out to each side, elbows at 45°. Bring them together at the top without clinking.
Complements the bench press for full chest development.
Bench or step to elevate the feet. The higher the feet, the more the upper chest works.
Feet on the bench, hands on the floor. Same execution as standard push-ups.
Advanced push-up variant that targets the upper chest.
Arms open, elbows slightly bent. Lower in an arc. Bring back up while squeezing.
A burning sensation = good sign. Light and precise.
Lat pulldown machine. Thighs locked under the pads. Wide bar.
Pull the bar to the TOP of the chest (never behind the neck). Squeeze the shoulder blades for 2 sec. Torso fixed.
Builds the V-taper. Drive elbows toward your back pockets.
Olympic bar on the floor. Alternative: Smith machine.
Torso at 45°, back FLAT. Pull the bar toward the navel. Elbows travel behind the back. Squeeze shoulder blades 1 sec.
Builds back thickness. Rounded back = too heavy.
Fixed pull-up bar. Use an assisted machine if needed.
Pronated grip (palms forward) wider than the shoulders. Pull until your chin clears the bar. 3-sec descent.
Best back exercise. Use assistance if you can\'t hit 8 reps.
High pulley + straight bar. Standing facing the pulley, slightly bent.
Arms nearly extended, pull the bar in an arc toward the thighs. Squeeze the back at the bottom. Controlled return.
Isolates the lats without biceps. Straight arms = key.
Low pulley with seat. V-handle (close grip).
Pull the handle toward the navel. Squeeze shoulder blades for 2 sec. Torso fixed, don\'t lean back.
Targets the rhomboids (mid-back) and improves posture.
1 dumbbell + flat bench for support (knee + hand).
Knee and hand on the bench, back flat. Pull the dumbbell toward the hip (not the shoulder). Elbow rises high.
Smith bar set at chest height. Or low rack bar.
Under the bar, body straight, feet on the floor. Pull the chest to the bar. Controlled descent.
Beginner version of the pull-up. Excellent for posture.
High pulley + rope. Standing facing the pulley.
Pull the rope toward your face while spreading your hands. Elbows high. Squeeze for 2 sec. End in a double-biceps pose.
Protects the shoulders and builds the rear delts.
Shoulder press machine. Seated, handles at ear level.
Press the handles overhead. Don\'t lock the elbows. Lower back down to ear level.
Dumbbells at ear level, elbows at 90°. Press overhead. Don\'t go below ear level. Abs braced.
Shoulders are fragile — load progressively. No back arch.
Floor. Push-up position with hips raised (inverted V shape).
Lower your head toward the floor by bending the elbows. Push back up. The higher the feet, the harder.
Progression toward the handstand push-up. Excellent for mass.
Light dumbbells or lateral raise machine.
Arms at your sides. Raise to horizontal. Elbows higher than the hands. 3-sec descent.
Builds shoulder width. Think \"elbows to the ceiling\". Light and strict.
Seated curl machine. Elbows on the support pad, supinated grip.
Curl the handles toward your shoulders. Squeeze for 1 sec. Controlled 2-sec descent.
Isolates the biceps perfectly, no cheating possible.
Elbows pinned to the body, FIXED. Curl up to the shoulders. 3-sec descent. Full extension at the bottom.
Pull-up bar. Supinated grip (palms toward you), shoulder-width.
Pull until your chin clears the bar. The biceps work more than in pronation.
Best biceps exercise. Also works the back.
Lying on the bench, arms hanging. Curl by bending the elbows. FULL 3-sec descent.
Builds the biceps peak. The bottom stretch is the key.
High pulley + rope or straight bar.
Facing the pulley, elbows pinned to the ribs. Push down. Spread the rope at the bottom. Squeeze for 1 sec.
Spreading the rope at the bottom recruits the long head (volume).
Lying down, arms extended. Bend the elbows to lower the bar toward the forehead. Elbows FIXED. Press back up.
Builds the triceps horseshoe. Precision movement.
Arms extended, lower until elbows reach 90°. Upright = triceps, leaned forward = pecs. Push back up.
If too hard, use the assisted machine. One of the best upper-body exercises.
Bent over, elbow at 90° against the body. Extend the arm back. Squeeze for 2 sec. Lower back down.
Triceps finisher. Light and controlled, burning sensation.
High pulley + rope. Kneeling facing the pulley.
Rope behind the head. Crunch the sternum toward the pubis. Hips do NOT move. Squeeze for 2 sec, exhale fully.
Best gym ab exercise. Progressively loadable.
Floor mat + weight plate (10–22 lb) held against the chest.
Lying down, knees bent, plate on chest. Crunch the shoulders up. Squeeze for 1 sec. Lower without resting.
Loaded version of the classic crunch. Easy progression.
Lying down, knees bent, hands behind the head (don\'t pull the neck). Crunch the shoulders up. Squeeze for 1 sec.
Basic but effective. 20+ reps with slow contraction.
Ab crunch machine (seated, handles in front).
Crunch the torso down against the resistance. Squeeze for 2 sec. Controlled return.
Guided and safe. Good alternative to the cable crunch.
Torso rotation machine. Seated, handles to the sides.
Rotate the torso side to side against the resistance. Control the movement.
Sculpts the obliques. Slow and controlled, no jerking.
Heavy dumbbell in each hand. Walk 100–130 ft keeping the torso perfectly upright. Abs braced.
Trains the transverse + obliques + forearms. Functional.
Raise the knees toward the chest by CURLING the pelvis. 3-sec descent. Without the curl = useless.
Targets the lower abs (below the navel). The pelvic curl is everything.
Plank: forearms + toes, 45–60 sec. Side plank: on your side, 30 sec/side. Body = straight line.
Strengthens the transverse (flat stomach) + obliques (slim waist).
Standing calf raise machine. Shoulders under the pads, balls of the feet on the edge.
Rise as high as possible on the toes. Squeeze for 2 sec. Lower the heels as far as possible. FULL range of motion.
Calves resist growth. Range of motion + volume = key.
Bar on the traps (squat rack) or dumbbells in hand + step.
Balls of the feet on the step, heels in the air. Raise/lower with maximum range of motion.
Progress to heavy loads. Calves can take a lot.
Stair step. One foot at a time for more intensity.
Ball of the foot on the step, heel in the air. Raise and lower slowly. 20 reps/foot.
One foot at a time doubles the intensity. Hold onto the wall.
Seated calf raise machine. Knees under the pads.
Rise on the toes, squeeze for 2 sec, lower heels low. Knees at 90°.
Targets the soleus (deep muscle). Complements the standing calf raise.
